BohrSet.statement: For an abelian group $G$ (an additive commutative group), $\mathrm{BohrSet}(G)$ is a type (in the same universe as $G$). According to its docstring, a Bohr set $B$ on $G$ is a finite set of characters of $G$ (the frequencies) together with an extended nonnegative real number for each frequency $\psi$ (the width of $B$ at $\psi$); $B$ is thought of as the set $\{x : \|1 - \psi(x)\| \le \mathrm{width}_B(\psi) \text{ for all frequencies } \psi\}$ (the chord-length convention, as opposed to the arc-length convention $|\arg \psi(x)| \le \mathrm{width}_B(\psi)$), and this set does not uniquely determine $B$ (neither its frequencies nor its widths).
